title: Molecular Dynamics Study on Wear Resistance of High Entropy Alloy Coatings Considering the Effect of Temperature

recollection.starting_material: Guess: Possibly a multi-element CoCrFeNi-based high-entropy alloy powder or substrate used for coating.
recollection.intervention: Guess: The study likely involved molecular dynamics simulations of wear under different temperature conditions.
recollection.structure: Guess: The resulting structure was presumably a densely packed, multi-element alloy layer on the substrate.
recollection.mechanism: Guess: Improved wear resistance potentially arose from the high configurational entropy and lattice distortion of the CoCrFeNi-based alloy, which hindered dislocation movement.
recollection.results: Guess: The paper may have reported lower wear rates at elevated temperatures, with quantitative measurements showing reduced friction and enhanced stability.

score.note: The recollection only generically identifies temperature-dependent molecular-dynamics wear simulations, which is already evident from the title. It omits the nanoindentation/friction protocol and temperatures. It does not recall the temperature-driven lattice disorder, dislocation-density changes, or HCP fraction. The proposed lattice-distortion mechanism is unsupported and the claimed improvement in wear at elevated temperature contradicts the reported sharp degradation above 900 K. No quantitative values are provided.
